data.exact_reserve_text: A detailed review by line of business has been performed. This has resulted in an explicit uplift to reserves to allow for anticipated claims inflation. Nevertheless, net reserve releases contributed a GBP 4.7m profit (Prior: n/a) for the year.
data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 1254 commenced operations in 2022 and assumed legacy liabilities via an inwards RITC for 2017-2019. The gross claims provision at 1 January 2022 was effectively nil (first year of operation); the inwards RITC added GBP 75.257m gross of reserves which were subsequently reduced by a gross release of GBP 27.481m in the year (plus a foreign exchange uplift), producing a closing gross claims outstanding of GBP 55.574m. The managing agent cites an explicit uplift to reserves to allow for anticipated claims inflation but reports net reserve releases contributing a GBP 4.7m profit. Overall movement is therefore a release, driven by favourable development offsetting inflationary provisioning.

net reserve releases contributed a GBP 4.7m profit (Prior: n/a) for the year.
Reserve releases in excess of claim payments will generate profits for the Syndicate and vice versa.

During 2022, the global economy saw a considerable increase in the rate of inflation. While the Syndicate has seen little direct evidence of claims inflation, there may be considerable delays before current inflation manifests itself in future claim payments.

data.data_quality_notes: Opening reserves at 1 Jan 2022 are zero because this is the Syndicate's first year of operation and the technical movement table shows an inwards RITC adding GBP 75.257m gross on 1 Jan 2022. The gross prior-year movement used is the 'Change in the provision for claims in the year' line from the claims movement note (-GBP 27.481m gross, a release). There is no separate 'movement in prior year's provision' line explicitly isolating only pre-2020 years; however the syndicate has no current underwriting years, so the change in provision is effectively prior-year movement. Lob-level movements are taken from the 'Gross claims incurred' column by LOB in the segmental table (these are P&L claims-incurred figures rather than an explicit per-LOB reserve-movement reconciliation) and so should be treated as indicative only.
